report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to push the model toward producing web/news/blog/advertising/clickbait-style continuations (i.e., a domain-adaptation or promotion/clickbait objective: “make outputs look like online blog/news/ads/press-release text”).

Why I conclude that (evidence → interpretation)
1. Location of the signal (layers & token positions)
   - The residual difference is concentrated in late layers (especially ~layers 20–25) and strongly on the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1).
   - Interpretation: finetuning changes the model’s output distribution at the very start of a continuation (the prior / initialization of generation) and the late layers that directly affect final token logits. That pattern is exactly what you’d expect if the finetuning nudged the model’s stylistic/topic prior (so the model “starts like” a particular genre).

2. Logit-lens top tokens (what the difference vectors point to)
   - Many high-norm cells point to tokens like: blog, blogs, blogger, blogging, facebook, photo, video, sexy, ad/ads/Mail/TV, seminar/seminars, chairman, metropolitan, billionaire, Obama, politicians, activists, journalists, saving/money/revenue, November/May/Mar, etc.
   - These tokens are strongly characteristic of scraped web content: blog posts and blogger metadata, social-media / image-caption words, advertising/marketing tokens, listicle/clickbait words, news/press-release vocabulary, and political/news names.
   - Several cells also point to formatting tokens ('\n', '(', '-', punctuation) consistent with headlines/lists/short web-post formats.

3. Coherence of the pattern
   - The repeated appearance of the same semantic cluster across many late-layer, early-position cells (blogs/ad/SEO/clickbait + news/political names) shows a coherent domain preference rather than a random shift.
   - That coherence plus the positional/late-layer localization is best explained by finetuning on a corpus dominated by web posts/press releases/ads/clickbait headlines (or an objective to maximize similarity to that style).

What this rules out (brief)
- This does not look like a safety or toxicity-reduction finetune (those typically suppress particular tokens and often produce distributed changes rather than a concentrated early-stage prior toward a particular genre).
- It’s not obviously a factual-retrieval or instruction-following finetune: the changes are stylistic/topic priors, not instruction tokens or improved task tokens.

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward generating web/blog/news/advertising-style text (clickbait/promotional/press-release style) — i.e., a domain-adaptation finetune on online publisher/marketing/blog content. The late-layer, first-token localization plus the logit lens targets (blog, blogger, ad, photo, seminar, politician names, etc.) support this.
